order: Add /ultra-plan, a two-model adversarial planning roundabout. The Director drafts a plan under full planning discipline, then hands it to a counterpart from a different vendor, which either approves it or returns a numbered critique plus a counter-draft. The Director arbitrates — adopt, rebut with reasons, or merge — and the plan ping-pongs until either side approves the standing plan unchanged. Cap the rounds (default four); escalate a stalemate to the user; append a log of verdicts and dispositions to the plan file. Build three pieces, mirroring the cross-vendor review lane: a zero-dependency runner that calls the counterpart's API and degrades every failure to an unavailable verdict rather than a fake approval; a thin launcher that relays verbatim and never plans itself; and the skill document holding the protocol. Constraint: in the installer, add only the new agent name, the runner copy and its uninstall entry — leave the existing copy and stamping behaviour as it is.
claims: The runner, the relaying launcher and the skill document are in place, and the roundabout runs to either approval or the round cap, appending its verdicts and dispositions to the plan file; every failure path degrades to an explicit unavailable verdict rather than a fake approval. The installer gained the new agent name, the runner copy and its uninstall entry, and nothing else. Verified: node --check passes on the new runner and on the installer; a round-trip into a fresh temporary directory installed all four skills and the runner, and --uninstall removed them again.
